name: How important is the building's reserve study when buying an oceanfront condo?

mainEntity.name: How important is the building's reserve study when buying an oceanfront condo?

acceptedAnswer.text: The building's reserve study is a crucial document that evaluates the long-term financial health of the homeowner association. It assesses the condition of major common elements (like the roof, elevators, and seawall) and projects their replacement costs and expected lifespan. The study then recommends how much the HOA should have in its reserve fund to cover these future expenses without relying heavily on special assessments. A well-funded reserve indicates proactive management and can save owners from unexpected, large out-of-pocket costs, making it a key decision factor in assessing the true value and future stability of your investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: The reserve study assesses the building's financial health, projecting future repair costs and the adequacy of HOA reserves. A well-funded reserve can prevent large special assessments.
